Now with him was his son, Malik al-Mansur;
this man fortified himself in Mayperqat,
and sent to Saladin and said to him:
that if he did not leave with him the regions of his father, Taqi al-Din,
he would ally with Bukhtamar, the lord of Khilat.
For this reason, Saladin ignored him for the moment,
and after a little while he gave the regions of his father to al-Adil,
and to him, to Malik
al-Mansur, he gave Edessa, Harran, and Samosata.
And while both camps, of the Franks and of the Arabs, were encamped against Ascalon,
one day while they were staying there, the Arabs set an ambush for the Franks who were going out from the camp to gather wood.
And when the Franks saw the ambush that was revealed,
each one mounted his horse
and fell upon the ambush of the Arabs.
And they killed three of the chief men among the servants of Saladin,
while from the Franks only two horsemen of ordinary rank were captured.
And the king of England (Angletar) sent an envoy to al-Adil,
and blamed him concerning the ambush.
And he said to him further:
"I desire to see you and to speak with you."
And the Franks pitched a large tent outside of their camp,
and al-Adil went to the king of England,
and sat there the whole day,
and toward evening they separated from each other.
And the king said to al-Adil:
"I desire also to sit thus in this tent with the Sultan, your brother,
and to see him and to speak with him."
And when al-Adil told Saladin,
he was not willing for two reasons:
first, that he was afraid,
and second, that he would not demean himself {OCR?} to go to that one.
Therefore he replied:
"It is not fitting for kings to gather together except after the confirmation of peace;
and lo, it is not yet confirmed.
And if we should consider that it is confirmed,
I do not understand his speech,
nor he mine.
And it is necessary that an interpreter be between us;
therefore, let him make the envoy an interpreter,
and there is no need for a meeting."
And when it became winter,
the king of England went to Acre,
and Saladin went to Jerusalem,
and he sent twenty-four thousand gold dinars,
and with them he ransomed the Arab captives from the hands of the Franks.
